Hi Leah — thanks for flagging and for the usage CSV, that helps. We looked into the incident and here's what we have so far:

- Root cause: a client-side cache misconfiguration caused a burst of identical requests with full context that bypassed their prefix cache; this amplified token traffic by roughly 9x for the 08:00–11:00 PT window. Our autoscaling and quota guards operated as designed but the quota thresholds were exceeded before we could trigger a softened throttle path.

- Immediate remediation options we can offer:
  * One-time goodwill credit of 40% of the billed overrun for the Nov 28 event (applied to your Dec invoice), OR
  * Spread the overrun as a phased true-up across two invoices (50% Dec / 50% Jan) with no extra finance fees.

- Long-term guard: we recommend a short-term temporary headroom reservation (ephemeral pool) sized to cover launch-day multipliers and a safety-net throttling configuration. That can be enabled for the next 30 days and then reviewed.

Ben (CC'd) can propose exact numbers and finalize with Procurement. If you prefer a single call to close, I'm available Tues 11/31 10:00–11:00 PT (or Wed morning).

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0191

2) Phased true-up option: If you'd rather avoid a single large adjustment, we can instead split the remaining balance 50% on Dec invoice / 50% on Jan invoice. Either way there will be no finance fees or interest.

3) Temporary headroom (recommended): We can provision a 30-day ephemeral pool sized to cover 10x baseline traffic for launch windows. LaunchCo gets a 25% discount on the ephemeral pool price if you commit to using it within the next 7 days.
